I have attached a screenshot and a photo confirming my purchase of the product from Amazon in March of 2025. Tue, Mar 10, 2:56 PM (2 days ago)
	
	
to Intel
I can try, but I can assure you Amazon is not going to care, as your company does not. Falsely claiming my product is fake and saying that you're keeping it is simply theft. I now feel compelled to contact the BBB and sign onto the class action lawsuit against your company. I will never purchase Intel again, and I will compel everyone I know to jump ship to AMD, as I will. Now I will take to forums to spread my story. The fact that you are unwilling to even reassess the situation is mind-boggling. And again, this is a well-documented tactic your company takes to try to cheat honest and loyal customers out of their hard-earned money because you made faulty products that you are unwilling to stand by. This has to be the worst customer service experience I've ever had in my entire life. Shame on Intel.

Why would I even have a fake processor? How and where does one acquire such a thing? How widespread of a problem could this possibly be? Is it possible that Amazon themselves sourced bad processors from an unreliable source? Also, why did I get an email claiming the RMA is canceled due to the product not being received, whenever you say it's because it is counterfeit?
